result.title: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints
result.comment: Accepted to EMNLP 2026 (Main Conference). 24 pages. Project page: https://igg-bench.github.io/
result.summary: GUI grounding benchmarks ask whether an agent can localize a target that is already visible in a static screenshot. Real interfaces often violate this assumption: a target may be off-screen, appear only after a state change or hover, remain occluded, or become actionable after a delay. This leaves the ability to recover target visibility unevaluated. To measure this reveal step, we introduce Interactive GUI Grounding (IGG), a benchmark in which an agent must first make the target visible through interaction and then click it. IGG contains 601 tasks across 16 controllable GUI environments and seven visibility-constraint sub-types, with a compact action space of scrolling, moving, dragging, waiting, and clicking. In our human study, participants achieve 94.6% accuracy, while GPT-5.5 reaches 79.4% and the strongest evaluated open-source VLM reaches only 31.6%. To identify the source of this gap, we conduct two controlled interventions. Telling Qwen3-VL which interaction to perform raises its accuracy only from 30.8% to 33.9%, whereas performing the interaction for the model raises it to 81.9%. The bottleneck is executing the reveal interaction, not recognizing the target once it is exposed. We further show that this capability is learnable, demonstrating that visibility recovery can be strengthened consistently across model families.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 IGG 基准，覆盖 16 个可控 GUI 环境、601 个任务与七类可见性约束，要求智能体先用滚动、悬停、拖拽、等待等交互使目标显现再点击定位，并通过人类对比与两组干预定位能力缺口。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接考察「先获取视觉证据再决策」的 LOOK 环节；其干预显示瓶颈在执行揭示交互而非识别已暴露目标，可供核查视觉证据获取成本与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 收益分配的关系。
